items.title: Perak police probe sexual harassment allegations against PKNPk CEO
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 13 — Perak police have opened an investigation into alleged slander involving sexual harassment claims against Perak State Development Corporation (PKNPk) chief executive officer Datuk Redza Rafiq Abdul Razak, following a report lodged by the corporation. State police chief commissioner Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the investigation was initiated based on the police report lodged by PKNPk over the matter, which had been circulated on social media. Mohd Alwi said police had yet to receive any report from the alleged sexual harassment victim.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia stays lower at midday
items.summary: Among the heavyweights, CIMB Group gained four sen to RM7.96, while Maybank shed two sen to RM10.58, Public Bank eased three sen to RM5.16, IHH Healthcare slid four sen each to RM5.15 and Tenaga Nasional was six sen lower to RM14.52. On the most active list, Key ASIC added three sen to 6.5 sen, Ekovest was half a sen higher at 20.5 sen, Oppstar rose three sen to 71.5 sen, and HHRG inched up half a sen to 16 sen, while NationGate eased three sen to RM1.53. As for the top losers, Hong Leong Bank fell 34 sen to RM22.36, United Plantations slid 28 sen to RM33.32, PPB Group dropped 17 sen to RM9.36, Malaysia Smelting Corporation lost 16 sen to RM2.06 and Fraser & Neave erased 14 sen to RM26.76.

items.title: Malaysia's natural rubber output jumps 31.5pct in June
items.summary: On a year-on-year basis, production increased 1.2 per cent from 26,249 tonnes. Malaysia's NR stocks also increased 5.2 per cent month-on-month to 129,524 tonnes in June from 123,149 tonnes in May. Rubber processors held 77.8 per cent of total stocks, followed by rubber consumers at 22.1 per cent and rubber estates at 0.1 per cent.

items.title: Gamuda bags RM1.64bil solar, battery contracts in Australia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd has clinched engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contracts worth a combined A$569 million (RM1.64 billion) for two solar and battery hybrid projects in Queensland, Australia. The construction firm said its Australian unit, DT Infrastructure Pty Ltd (DTI), had entered into the EPC contracts for the Ganymirra and Majors Creek projects. Once operational, the projects are expected to support Queensland's renewable energy transition by providing renewable power generation backed by large-scale battery storage.

items.title: Alam Flora regrets impact, pledges safety focus as Pantai Hillpark lorry crash probe continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Alam Flora has pledged its full cooperation with authorities in the probe into a crash involving one of its compactor garbage lorries along Jalan Pantai Murni 1, Pantai Hillpark, yesterday. In a statement today, Alam Flora informed that the vehicle will be sent for inspection to identify the exact cause of the incident, in line with instructions from the investigating officer. “We deeply regret the impact this incident has had on the affected community and remain committed to ensuring high safety standards in all our operational activities,” the statement read.

items.title: Malaysia's labour demand grows 1.7pct to 9.25mil jobs in Q2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's labour demand grew 1.7 per cent year-on-year to 9.25 million jobs in the second quarter of 2026 despite global uncertainties, the Statistics Department said. The department said 97.9 per cent of the jobs were filled, while the remaining 2.1 per cent were vacancies. Filled jobs rose 1.7 per cent to 9.05 million from 8.9 million a year earlier, led by the services sector, which grew 2.4 per cent and accounted for 53.4 per cent, or 4.83 million, of the total.

items.title: MN Holdings bags RM71mil TNB contract in Cameron Highlands
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MN Holdings Bhd's subsidiary MN Power Transmission Sdn Bhd has secured a RM71.02 million contract from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to establish a new 132/33 kilovolt (kV) transmission main intake (PMU) in Blue Valley, Cameron Highlands, Pahang. MN Holdings said the contract took effect on Aug 12, 2026, with completion scheduled within 900 days from the commencement date. Under the contract, MN Power Transmission is required to provide a performance security of RM3.551 million, equivalent to five per cent of the accepted contract value, within 56 days from the contract date.

items.title: Meth, heroin and cannabis worth RM18,500 found inside a Lumut police cell, and a cop's in trouble too
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 13 — Three men, including a police constable, were arrested after police seized drugs worth RM18,534 at the Lumut police station lock-up in Manjung. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the drugs were found during an inspection of the lock-up on Tuesday at about 8.30am. He said police found 16 small plastic tubes containing 109g of methamphetamine, 16 plastic tubes containing 110g of heroin and 23 tubes containing 142g of dried cannabis leaves.

items.title: Poor response to subsidised health check scheme for commercial drivers - Loke
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Transport Ministry's subsidised health screening programme for commercial vehicle drivers has received a poor response, with fewer than 20 drivers participating within a month of its launch. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the low uptake was disappointing, particularly as the programme was introduced to improve driver health and road safety while reducing the financial burden of medical examinations. Loke said many drivers continued to opt for the manual medical examination process, raising concerns over the ministry's ability to verify whether the existing approach was effectively improving drivers' health.

items.title: TH Act amendments being refined, consultations ongoing, says minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act are being refined in consultation with various stakeholders, says Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan. He said the changes will incorporate recommendations made by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Zulkifli previously told the Dewan Rakyat that the proposed amendments would cover the regulatory framework for TH's fund management and investments.

items.title: 25 companies seek financing under Penang climate mitigation fund
items.summary: Chief minister Chow Kon Yeow said the fund, established under the Penang Green Industry Programme in partnership with Alliance Bank, has an initial allocation of RM20 million, comprising RM5 million from the state government and RM15 million from the bank, with a potential commitment of up to RM100 million. Chow said the shift towards clean energy is no longer simply an environmental concern but increasingly a competitiveness issue, particularly as global companies set stronger carbon targets across their supply chains. For Penang's manufacturers, clean energy is no longer simply an environmental issue.

items.title: Jobstreet: Firms still keen on hiring, job ads grew 33pc year-on-year
items.summary: “Jobstreet’s platform data reflects continued hiring demand. In H1 2026, job ads increased by 33 per cent year-on-year, showing that employers are still actively looking for talent across the market,” said Nicholas Lam, managing director, Jobstreet by SEEK Malaysia. Manufacturing, transport and logistics accounted for the largest share of job ads at 12 per cent, followed by accounting at 11 per cent, sales at 10 per cent, engineering at 9 per cent, and administration and office support at 8 per cent, the platform said citing its internal data.

items.title: ‘I am very relaxed’: Loke dismisses talk of final ministry assembly before DAP congress decision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today played down suggestions that this could be his last monthly assembly with Transport Ministry staff ahead of DAP’s crucial vote on Sunday on whether the party should remain in the federal government. Asked whether today’s ministry assembly could be his final one with ministry staff, Loke dismissed the assumption. Asked if he was nervous ahead of the DAP special congress on Sunday, Loke said he was relaxed.

items.title: Transport minister urges commercial vehicle drivers to make RM30 health screening count as fewer than 20 sign up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Fewer than 20 commercial vehicle drivers have taken up the government’s subsidised health screening programme since it was launched last month, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said today. Loke said the programme was aimed at improving the health and wellbeing of drivers, particularly those responsible for carrying passengers and operating commercial vehicles. Loke urged drivers, particularly older ones, to undergo comprehensive health screenings to identify potential health problems early.

items.title: MACC's domestic probe into KWAP-eFishery investment nearly 80pct complete
items.summary: KUCHING: The domestic component of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) probe into KWAP's RM163.4 million investment in Indonesian aquaculture firm eFishery is nearly 80 per cent complete. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the international phase would take longer as investigators still require information and evidence from several foreign jurisdictions. "To date, the domestic investigation has reached almost 80 per cent, while the investigation at the international level is still ongoing," he told a press conference here today.

items.title: MACC completes probes into three TH RCI issues, submits recommendations
items.summary: KUCHING: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has completed investigations into three of the six original issues arising from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji, with recommendations for charges and no further action (NFA) submitted. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said investigations into the remaining three issues were also near completion. "Of the six issues, three have been completed.

items.title: Kelana Jaya LRT services return to normal after power outage
items.summary: Rapid KL, in a Facebook post, said the technical glitch, which occurred at 9.28am, left a train stranded between the Taman Jaya and Universiti stations. The rail operator said alternative train services had been ended and passengers safely evacuated from the stranded train in accordance with its standard operating procedures. "Passengers inside the affected train were safely transferred to a rescue train before being brought to a nearby station," Rapid KL said.

items.title: Kelana Jaya LRT services fully restored after power outage near University station
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Kelana Jaya LRT services returned to normal at 10.25am today after a power supply disruption at Universiti station left a train stranded between Taman Jaya and Universiti stations, Rapid KL said. The rail operator said the disruption began at about 9.28am, prompting passengers on the affected train to be transferred to a rescue train under established safety procedures. Rapid KL said the passengers subsequently continued their journeys on another train, with no injuries reported.

items.title: MACC uncovers eight more investment issues in TH RCI probe
items.summary: KUCHING: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has uncovered eight additional investment-related issues in its probe linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Halim told a press conference that the eight additional issues primarily involved investments and related decisions. "The second concerns a property investment under Abraj Sdn Bhd."

items.title: Passenger falls onto tracks at Gombak LRT station, causing brief Kelana Jaya Line disruption, says Rapid KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Explaining a brief disruption to Kelana Jaya LRT services this morning, Rapid KL said a passenger believed to have fainted fell onto the tracks at Gombak station at about 9.05am. The rail operator said the incident prompted the station’s Platform Intrusion Emergency Stop (PIES) system to be activated and power to the tracks to be temporarily cut. “Immediately after the incident, the Platform Intrusion Emergency Stop (PIES) system was activated and power supply to the tracks was temporarily cut off as a safety measure to allow the operations team and auxiliary police to take immediate action,” it said in a statement.

items.title: Farage and Count Binface go head-to-head in snap UK poll
items.summary: LONDON: Voters in eastern England head to the polls Thursday for a by-election triggered by hard-right Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, but amid a boycott by mainstream parties his main rival is a joke candidate called Count Binface. Brexit backer Farage – whose anti-immigration Reform UK won local elections in May and topped national polls for 18 months from early last year – has remained defiant. "Britain needs Reform, Britain wants Reform, and Britain demands a general election," he said in a statement late Wednesday.

items.title: Khaled says navy personnel safe following training incident in South China Sea
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) personnel were involved in an incident following a free-fall parachuting exercise in the South China Sea yesterday. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin confirmed the matter when contacted by the New Straits Times. Khaled, however, did not indicate the nature of the incident nor the number of personnel involved.

items.title: JPJ taps BoBoiBoy, PapaZola to help push road safety campaigns to Gen Z and younger audiences
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) is teaming up with local animation studio Monsta Studios to bring road safety messages to younger Malaysians through animation and digital content. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the collaboration was part of efforts to strengthen the country’s road safety agenda by using digital content, animation, social media and creative storytelling to deliver safety messages. “The collaboration between JPJ and Monsta Studios, which combines JPJ’s expertise in road safety and road regulations with Monsta Studios’ strengths in animation, creative content and digital communication, will ensure that road safety messages are understood, embraced and ultimately practised by the public,” he added Loke said traditional advertising methods such as billboards, television and newspapers were becoming less effective amid declining viewership and readership, making digital content increasingly important in reaching younger audiences.

items.title: Power outage at Universiti station causes Kelana Jaya LRT delays
items.summary: Rapid KL also announced temporary platform closures at several nearby stations to facilitate maintenance work. Platform 2 at the Taman Bahagia and Taman Paramount stations was temporarily closed, while Platform 1 at the Taman Jaya station was similarly closed. Passengers at Taman Bahagia and Taman Paramount stations were instructed to use Platform 1, while those at Taman Jaya station were required to board trains using Platform 2.

items.title: Loke: Govt agencies needs to adapt communication strategies to reach younger Malaysians
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Road Transport Department (RTD) has teamed up with Monsta Studios Sdn Bhd to deliver road safety messages through animation, creative content and digital communications, in a bid to better reach younger Malaysians. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the collaboration reflected the need for government agencies to adapt their communication strategies to reach their audiences. He said conventional methods such as billboards, television advertisements and newspaper advertisements had their limitations, making creative digital content increasingly important.

items.title: Penang Pakatan sticking with BN, Umno despite criticism, says Chow Kon Yeow
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 13 — Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) is sticking with its decision to continue working with Barisan Nasional (BN), including Umno, despite criticism from DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng, state PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said today. Chow said the decision remained Penang PH’s position and was not challenged during a state DAP internal engagement session held yesterday. Chow, who is also Penang chief minister, was responding to questions over the state DAP leadership’s continued cooperation with BN and Umno.

items.title: DAP leadership engages northern delegates ahead of National Congress
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: About 400 DAP delegates from Penang, Kedah and Perlis attended an engagement session with party secretary-general Anthony Loke and the Central Executive Committee (CEC) leadership here last night. The session, held ahead of the party's national congress on Aug 16, served as a platform for delegates to exchange views on party affairs, national issues and the party's future direction. The upcoming congress is expected to see delegates deliberate on the party's position and future direction within the Unity Government.

items.title: Tun M backs F1 return to Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia should consider reclaiming its hosting rights for Formula 1 (F1) as changes in currency values have made hosting fees more manageable today, said former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad. Dr Mahathir said while rising costs forced the country to drop off the F1 calendar in 2017, the financial equation had since shifted. In the past, RM100 million was huge, but today RM100 million feels like RM50 million used to," he said during the DR.M podcast.

items.title: Penang PH sticks to decision to accept BN, Umno
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang Pakatan Harapan remains committed to its decision to accept Barisan Nasional and Umno despite criticism from DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng. Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said the decision was not questioned during a recent engagement session involving the state coalition. Chow was responding to Lim's criticism of Penang PH's decision to accept BN and Umno, despite Lim describing statements by the two parties as unreasonable.

items.title: Loke: "Do I look nervous?...I am very relaxed"
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said it was premature to speculate on his position as Transport Minister or the status of his party ahead of the DAP National Congress this Sunday. Speaking to reporters here after a ministry function, Loke said he was "very relaxed" ahead of the party's National Congress. He dismissed questions that today's Transport Ministry assembly could be his last.

items.title: Penang may advise schools to suspend outdoor activities if air quality worsens, says CM
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 13 — The Penang government may advise schools to suspend or postpone outdoor activities if air quality in the state worsens, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. He said Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in Penang remained at moderate levels for now, but the state government was closely monitoring the situation. He said postponing outdoor activities at schools was among the measures that could be considered should air pollution worsen.

items.title: Israel carries out first Gaza strike in more than week, one killed
items.summary: GAZA CITY: Israel on Wednesday carried out its first air strike in more than a week in Gaza, both sides said, breaking a relative lull as the United States pressed a peace plan. The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas commander, charging that he had been planning attacks against Israeli forces operating in the war-battered territory. Gaza's civil defence agency, a rescue service under Hamas, said the strike in Beit Lahia in the northern Gaza Strip targeted civilians riding in a tuk-tuk.

items.title: VSTECS shares rise 3.42pct in early trade after firmer Q2 results
items.summary: At 10.17am, its shares gained six sen to RM1.81 with 5.23 million shares traded. The information technology provider posted a 50 per cent increase in net profit to RM30.31 million from RM20.17 million in the same period a year ago, driven by growth across all business segments. The performance was driven by higher sales across all three business segments -- information and communications technology (ICT) distribution, enterprise systems, and ICT services.

items.title: Thai mother's RM1,500 journey back to work in Johor ends in arrest
items.summary: TUMPAT: A Thai mother's attempt to return to her workplace in Malaysia after spending time with her children in Pattani ended with her arrest for illegal entry yesterday. However, her journey ended when she was detained by a General Operations Force (GOF) task force from the Seventh Battalion in Tanah Merah for entering Malaysia without valid travel documents. Nadia said she had returned to her hometown in Pattani last month to care for her children after her two-year-old twins fell ill. She said she later decided to return to Malaysia to resume work and earn a living for her three children.

items.title: Medan Pasar set for climate-resilient revamp under KL ‘sponge city’ push, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Historic Medan Pasar in downtown Kuala Lumpur is set for a revamp aimed at improving rainwater management and public accessibility while preserving its heritage identity, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said today. In a Facebook post, Yeoh said the project is a collaboration between Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and Yayasan Creador, with the public space to be made more open, accessible and welcoming to the community. “This project embraces Nature-based Solutions, with improved rainwater management.”

items.title: South Korean shares hit 3-week high as chipmakers jump
items.summary: Shares of chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics rallied more than 7 per cent and 5 per cent, respectively. Among other South Korean index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution climbed 1.95 per cent, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were up 2.93 per cent and up 1.62 per cent, respectively. Steelmaker POSCO Holdings shed 0.08 per cent, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics rose 0.84 per cent.

items.title: South Korea unveils package to boost housing supply, support young buyers
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea said on Thursday it would raise financial support for construction projects and ease regulations for young homebuyers as part of efforts to stabilise a red-hot housing market. Lee's approval ratings have been falling on rising house prices and stock market volatility. The FSC said it would raise policy support for financing construction projects to 47.8 trillion won (US$33.72 billion) or more, from a planned 26.3 trillion won, to boost housing supply.

items.title: [UPDATED] Soldier injured in Port Dickson firing range mishap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A soldier was injured in a shooting mishap at a firing range in Port Dickson during a live-fire drill. The Army Strategic Communication Branch said the incident occurred at 2.15pm yesterday at the firing range in Menyala, Port Dickson, while soldiers were undergoing training for the Malaysian Army Shooting Skills Test (UKMTD) competition. Akhmal was rushed to Port Dickson Hospital for initial treatment.

items.title: Oil drops on lower demand forecasts despite deadlock in US-Iran talks
items.summary: BEIJING: Oil prices fell more than US$1 on Thursday as forecasters lowered global oil demand projections for 2026 because of the disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran, though the supply constraints from the conflict provided a floor for the market. Brent futures dropped US$1.29, or 1.5 per cent, at US$87.69 a barrel by 0100 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell US$1.30, or 1.6 per cent, to US$81.97.

items.title: Yuan at 3-1/2-year high as US inflation dims Fed rate hike prospects
items.summary: SHANGHAI: China's yuan firms to a 3-1/2-year high against the dollar on Thursday, as US inflation data weighed on the greenback and dimmed prospects for an imminent Federal Reserve rate hike. US consumer prices were in line with expectations, easing appreciation pressure on the dollar in the near term and lending the yuan a broadly steady to slightly firmer bias, market participants said. It hit 6.74 per dollar in early trade, the strongest since February 2023.

items.title: Venezuela govt, opposition wrap up round of post-Maduro talks
items.summary: CARACAS: Venezuela's interim government and opposition representatives on Wednesday wrapped up a first round of talks aimed at reconciling the nation following the US ouster of longtime leader Nicolas Maduro. Under Maduro, Venezuela had tried repeatedly and unsuccessfully to access the funds. Interim president Delcy Rodriguez's government was represented at the talks by her brother Jorge Rodriguez, who is also the head of Venezuela's National Assembly.

items.title: Illegals busted running gambling outlet under guise of grocery shop
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has busted an illegal gambling operation disguised as a grocery shop in Taman Serdang Perdana, Seri Kembangan. Immigration officers who got wind of the gambling den raided the place yesterday and detained six individuals, including a woman believed to be the caretaker, three Bangladeshi men and two Indonesian women, aged between 20 and 45. The operation began at 3pm and followed a month-long intelligence operation based on public information and surveillance.

items.title: Power outage at University station disrupts Kelana Jaya LRT services
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Kelana Jaya LRT services are experiencing delays this morning after a power outage at University station left a train unable to operate. As part of the disruption management, Platform 2 at Taman Bahagia and Taman Paramount stations has been temporarily closed for maintenance, while Platform 1 at Taman Jaya station is also closed. Passengers at Taman Bahagia and Taman Paramount have been advised to use Platform 1 to board trains, while those at Taman Jaya should use Platform 2.

items.title: Unhealthy air quality recorded in 11 areas nationwide, Sarawak worst hit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — As of 9am today, air quality in 11 areas across the country is at unhealthy levels, with Sarawak reporting the most affected areas. Meanwhile, 55 areas recorded moderate API readings of between 51 and 100, while two other areas registered good air quality below 50. API readings from 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51—100 moderate, 101—200 unhealthy, 201—300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 are classified as hazardous.

items.title: Seven areas in Sarawak record unhealthy API levels, down from nine
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 13 — Seven areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollution Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze as of 8am this morning, compared to nine areas yesterday morning. Based on the Air Pollution Index Management System (APIMS), the areas recording unhealthy API readings are Samarahan (183), Serian (183), Kuching (177), Sri Aman (159), Sarikei (158), Mukah (152) and Sibu (152). The API data is released hourly, based on 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Soldier suffers facial injuries after being accidentally shot during Port Dickson firing practice
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 13 — A soldier suffered facial injuries after being accidentally shot by a colleague at a firing range in Sungai Menyala, Port Dickson, yesterday. Negeri Sembilan Police deputy chief SAC Mohd Nasharudin Mohd Shariff said the incident occurred at about 2.15pm when the victim, who is in his 20s, and several other personnel were taking part in a shooting practice. “The victim was taken to Port Dickson Hospital before being transferred to Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital here for further treatment.

items.title: Former auditor-general says ‘right to be heard’ denied after not called to testify by Tabung Haji RCI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Former Auditor-General Tan Sri Madinah Mohamad reportedly said she was disappointed she was not called to testify before the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), despite turning up at the designated venue and being ready to give evidence. Madinah said she believed her right to be heard had been denied despite her attendance at the proceedings. Madinah defended her handling of the 2017 accounts, saying the EOMs were used to draw attention to material matters identified during the audit.

items.title: Port Klang shophouse fire kills man and eight-year-old nephew, two others hospitalised
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 13 — A 66-year-old man and his eight-year-old nephew died, while two others suffered breathing difficulties in a fire involving a three-storey shophouse on Jalan Batu Unjur 9, Taman Bayu Perdana, Port Klang this afternoon. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 5.51pm and found the second floor of the Class A building, measuring about 20 x 70 square feet, 90 per cent damaged by the fire. “After the fire was extinguished, firefighters found the two victims in separate toilets at 6.33pm.

items.title: RM10 a trip: GOF arrests Kelantan labourer who allegedly ferried undocumented migrants from river to bus station
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 13 — For just a fee of RM10, a labourer allegedly moonlit as a transporter to ferry foreigners who entered Malaysia via un gazetted routes along Sungai Golok to a bus station. The local man was arrested alongside an Indonesian man during Ops Taring Wawasan Kelantan by the Sector A Strike Force, Company A of the 7th Battalion (General Operations Force), near Gate 1 of the Rantau Panjang Duty-Free Complex, Pasir Mas at approximately 10pm on Tuesday. “Preliminary interrogation revealed that the local man lives around Rantau Panjang and works as a labourer, besides doing part-time work as a transporter charging a fee of RM10 to ferry customers, usually foreigners, who entered via the river to the bus station.

items.title: Anwar mourns Zhu Rongji, remembers ‘good friend’ who helped deepen Malaysia-China ties
items.summary: Anwar described Zhu as one of the great architects of China’s economic transformation and a good friend, saying his reforms had helped accelerate the country’s rise as an economic superpower. It was Zhu’s reforms that helped accelerate China’s extraordinary rise as an economic superpower,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday. “In the 1990s, Zhu and I worked together to deepen economic and financial ties between Malaysia and China.

items.title: Dr Mahathir, Dr Siti Hasmah recognised with three records after both turn 100
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali have received three records recognising their longevity and unique achievements as a couple. The 101-year-old Dr Mahathir was recognised by Asean Records as the Oldest Living Former Prime Minister, while 100-year-old Dr Siti Hasmah received the title of Oldest Living Spouse of a Former Prime Minister. Dr Mahathir celebrated his 101st birthday on July 10, followed by Dr Siti Hasmah’s 100th birthday on July 12.

items.title: Proposed Mara Bill to impose term limits on board members under governance overhaul, says chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — About 80 per cent of the proposed Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) Bill 2026, to be tabled in Parliament before the end of the year, focuses on corporate governance aimed at strengthening the institution’s structure and management, said Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. “The Bill will also tighten financial governance and procurement practices to ensure they meet national and international standards,” he said. Asyraf Wajdi said the draft Bill would also establish several mandatory Board committees, including the Mara Audit, Investment, Finance and Governance, and Risk committees.

items.title: ‘Back home’: PM Anwar discharged after hernia surgery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim returned home yesterday after being discharged from hospital. In a Facebook post, Anwar uploaded a photo of himself reading a book with the caption “Alhamdulillah, back home”. Earlier, the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, was reported to have said that Anwar was expected to be discharged from hospital yesterday after receiving treatment.

items.title: When neutrality pays: How Malaysia is navigating the global fuel crisis
items.summary: Almost 40 per cent of Malaysia’s crude oil imports pass through the waterway, making any prolonged disruption a significant concern for the country’s energy security. Malaysia, a net importer of crude oil, produces about 350,000 barrels of oil a day but consumes about 700,000 barrels, according to the Finance Ministry. Malaysia also subsidises fuel for domestic consumption, keeping pump prices below those in some major oil-producing countries such as Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI report to go to police, MACC, Bank Negara, IRB for full investigation, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will go to the relevant authorities for a full investigation based on all findings and information contained in the report, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. “This includes information contained in the report, as well as additional information provided by Finance Minister II (Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan) and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting on the Tabung Haji RCI report, yesterday.” The TH RCI report was made public on July 29.

items.title: Two accused flee Kulim court, one slides down pillar to escape police
items.summary: KULIM, Aug 12 — Two men attending a case mention at the Kulim Magistrate’s Court here today fled the court compound after spotting police officers waiting to re-arrest them in connection with another case. Kulim police chief Supt Syamsul Sinring said the incident occurred at about 10am after both accused, aged 27 and 31, had completed their case mention and document submission. The case was fixed for re-mention on June 8, July 12 and today for document submission and case management,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Rubbish lorry crashes through Pantai Hillpark condo wall, crushes three cars
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — A rubbish lorry believed to have suffered brake failure lost control and crashed into a condominium boundary wall, crushing three cars at Jalan Pantai Murni 1, Pantai Hillpark, early today. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the lorry was travelling downhill along a straight, sloping road when the incident occurred at about 4.10am. The lorry driver, a 41-year-old local man, suffered an injury to his left leg, he said.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Prices of non subsidised RON97, RON95, diesel cheaper by 20, 15 and 10 sen respectively from Aug 13 to 19
items.summary: According to a statement by the Ministry of Finance (MoF), for the stated period, the price of RON97 is set at RM4.15 per litre compared to RM4.35 previously, while unsubsidised RON95 is priced at RM3.62 per litre compared to RM3.77, and unsubsidised diesel is set at RM4.47 per litre compared to RM4.57 previously. At the same time, subsidised petroleum prices remain unchanged at RM1.99 per litre for RON95 under Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) and RM2.10 per litre for diesel under Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel). Prices for the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and Subsidised Diesel Control Systems (SKDS) remain at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre , respectively.

items.title: Singapore fugitive flees to Johor, ends up kidnapped for S$80,000 ransom
items.summary: Federal Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. items.title: Five Chinese nationals arrested in Sri Petaling, Pudu over housebreakings in KL
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said investigations revealed that the suspects may have been involved in a housebreaking incident in Taman Desa Petaling on August 4, which caused the victim to suffer losses of about RM6,000 involving cash, jewelry, and a luxury-branded sling bag. “During the raid at approximately 9.30pm, the police also seized a vehicle along with various tools used for housebreaking,” he said in a statement today. Fadil said the police also recovered items belonging to the victim alongside various other luxury items including watches, wallets, and cash in various foreign currencies totalling more than RM10,000.
